sections.html: O. bernatziki can grow to a length of more than 10 cm, but usually stays much smaller (7-8 cm).

All Opsarius are peaceful schooling fish. Regarding aquarium biology, Opsarius can best be compared with Devario. However, Opsarius love a stronger current, so Opsarius species should be kept in a tank that reflects a biotope as found in a brook or small river.
Males of O. bernatziki can be recognized by the bigger head and larger fins.

For the first time ever we could import this pretty barb from Thailand. At first we thought the fish belonged to the species Opsarius ornatus, but after they had settled in, all of the fish showed a clearly marked caudal spot, which is typical for O. bernatziki but lacking in O. ornatus. Another very similar species from Thailand, O. signicaudus, also has a well marked caudal spot, but there it extends onto the caudal fin. Some scientists do not see Opsarius as a separate genus, but include all species mentioned here under Barilius.
